data.title: Valacyclovir
data.summary: IV Antivirals — Anti-herpes · L-valyl ester prodrug of acyclovir
data.body:
_Oral · IV Antivirals — Anti-herpes_

**Class:** L-valyl ester prodrug of acyclovir

## Mechanism of action
- Rapidly converted to acyclovir by first-pass intestinal and hepatic metabolism
- Then acts like acyclovir: viral thymidine kinase → triphosphate → inhibits viral DNA polymerase

## Pharmacokinetics
- Bioavailability about 55% (3–5 times that of acyclovir) → fewer daily doses
- Gives plasma acyclovir levels similar to IV acyclovir at high doses
- Renal excretion as acyclovir — reduce dose in renal impairment

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Herpes zoster (start within 72 h)
- Genital herpes: first episode, recurrences, suppression (also reduces transmission to partner)
- Herpes labialis (single-day treatment)
- HSV-associated erythema multiforme suppression

## Dose & formulations
- Herpes zoster: 1 g three times daily × 7 days
- First-episode genital herpes: 1 g twice daily × 7–10 days
- Recurrent genital herpes: 500 mg twice daily × 3 days, or 1 g once daily × 5 days
- Suppression: 500 mg–1 g once daily
- Herpes labialis: 2 g twice daily for 1 day (12 h apart)

## Adverse effects
- Headache, nausea, abdominal pain
- CNS toxicity (confusion, hallucinations) in elderly or renally impaired patients
- Very high doses (8 g/day) in advanced HIV/transplant: thrombotic microangiopathy (TTP/HUS)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity to valacyclovir or acyclovir

## Drug interactions
- As for acyclovir: probenecid, cimetidine, mycophenolate, nephrotoxic drugs

## Monitoring
- Renal function in the elderly or those with kidney disease

## Pregnancy & lactation
Considered safe (old FDA category B). Compatible with breastfeeding.

## Viva points
- A prodrug with 3–5 times better bioavailability than acyclovir
- Once-daily suppression; reduces genital herpes transmission
- TTP/HUS reported at very high doses in immunocompromised patients

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.11; Khopkar ch.3. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
